solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cavalry officer's last to wear flimsy stockings

indicators.note: the single letter puts the stockings on, so it sits inside the phrase for them

parts.note: light hose are thin, flimsy stockings

indicators.note: the final letter of the word officer is taken

explanation.surface: An army officer's final duty is to pull on a pair of sheer stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Light horse is a historical term for lightly armed mounted troops, a branch of cavalry.

clue.text: Left with old goods? One answer could be arcade

parts.note: G stands for good, doubled for the plural as with pp for pages
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone leaving with antique goods wonders whether an arcade is the place for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggia is an open-sided gallery with arches along one side, which is a kind of arcade.

clue.text: Threaten to go out and groove …

definitions.meaning: a candle flame flickers as if about to die
a channel cut for water to run along

explanation.surface: A threat to leave, trailing into the next clue, paired with a groove.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle flame that flickers low is said to do this, and the noun is a channel at a roadside or roof edge.

clue.text: … until you drop or until only the dregs are left

definitions.meaning: carrying on to the very last of your strength

definitions.text: until only the dregs are left
definitions.meaning: drinking a glass of beer down to its sediment

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, someone keeps going until exhausted, or drinks a glass right down.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of draught beer, so the second reading jokes that the phrase means drinking until the last of the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means persisting right to the finish however hard it gets, and the beer pun gives the second sense.

clue.text: A grade one fizzy drink

indicators.note: letters that fizz are bubbling about and so are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soft drink is awarded the top grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fizzy' reads as describing the drink, but it signals the shuffle of AGRADEONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet carbonated soft drink flavoured with orange.

clue.text: Dictator's requests to give up religious types

indicators.note: what someone dictating says aloud is heard, not seen, so a word that sounds alike is wanted

parts.note: seeks means asks for, requests

explanation.surface: A dictator's demands that people abandon their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant, but here it is a person dictating a letter, speaking words aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sikhs are followers of Sikhism, a monotheistic faith founded in the Punjab.

clue.text: Nigel Slater's filling does set

indicators.note: the answer is the filling inside these words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: The celebrity cook Nigel Slater's pie filling firms up properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Slater is a well-known British food writer and TV cook, which makes 'filling' and 'set' read as kitchen talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly or sauce that gels thickens and firms, which is what it does when it sets.

clue.text: Joins large numbers following England

indicators.note: the numbers come after the country, so they are placed second

parts.note: a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: Large crowds of people join up behind England.
explanation.definitionFit: To engraft is to graft one thing onto another, so it joins them together.

clue.text: Venue for summer show around end of August that's taken out of production

indicators.note: the summer venue goes round the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: seaside towns traditionally host summer variety shows on the pier

indicators.note: the final letter of the word August is taken

explanation.surface: A seaside resort's summer show closes at the end of August.
explanation.walkthrough: A British summer season of variety shows is staged at seaside resorts. Set-aside was the EU scheme paying farmers to leave land out of cultivation.
explanation.definitionFit: Set-aside farmland is deliberately left uncultivated, withdrawn from producing crops.

clue.text: Draught's her second new drink and their third — this could be letting off steam

definitions.text: this could be letting off steam

parts.note: draught in the sense of pulling a load, as in a draught horse, is traction

indicators.note: the letter in position two of the word her is taken

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: the letter in position three of the word their is taken

explanation.surface: Someone takes a beer, then a second drink, then another, and lets off steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draught' reads as beer, but it means hauling power.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam-powered road locomotive for hauling loads literally lets off steam as it works.

clue.text: It can be mean to tease

definitions.meaning: to imply or intend, as in what are you driving at
to needle or nag at someone

explanation.surface: Teasing can be unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to imply, as in 'what are you trying to say', and also to criticise or needle someone.

clue.text: N-N-N-Noah?

parts.note: Noah built the Ark, so he is its wright, and the stutter points to the stammering shopkeeper of the same name

explanation.surface: Someone stammers the name of the Biblical boat-builder.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkwright is the stammering corner-shop owner played by Ronnie Barker in the BBC sitcom Open All Hours; a wright is a maker, and Noah made the Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah was the maker, or wright, of the Ark, and the stutter adds the sitcom character with that surname.

clue.text: I caught bird back in the lettuce

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the bird's name is turned to read backwards

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: Someone catches a bird lurking at the back of the lettuce patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceberg is a crisp, pale variety of round lettuce.

clue.text: Gatherings from first-class lettuce rejected plus lettuces with no heart

indicators.note: the pair is sent back, so it reads backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here with I for the figure one
cos is a long-leaved lettuce

indicators.note: the middle of the word lettuces is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Fine lettuce is thrown out at parties, along with hollowed-out lettuces.
explanation.definitionFit: Socials are informal parties or get-togethers, gatherings of a club or group.

clue.text: Frustrated idiot snapped for a change

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A frustrated fool loses their temper for once.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let down when hopes are not met leaves one frustrated, a near synonym.

clue.text: Wise briefly to check repeated pressure in poor man's barometer

indicators.note: the shortened name blocks the pressure by sitting inside it

parts.note: pressure is given twice: as its abbreviation P and as the verb impel, to press forward

indicators.note: the first name is cut short to its familiar form, the way Eric Morecambe addressed his partner

parts.note: Ernie Wise, of the comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A wise person briefly checks a barometer repeatedly as the pressure changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' is Ernie Wise, the comedian partner of Eric Morecambe, who called him Ern. The scarlet pimpernel closes its flowers when rain is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is nicknamed the poor man's weatherglass because its flowers shut before bad weather.

clue.text: Withdraw score?

parts.note: to go back to one's house is to withdraw, and a footballer might score with his head in a home match

explanation.surface: A question about taking back a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, footballing reading: a goal headed into the net.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off back to one's house is to withdraw, while the words can also describe nodding a goal in.

clue.text: One's muscles are paramount for hard case?

indicators.note: the muscles come first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: abs and lats are two muscle groups, abdominals and latissimus
one has, i.e. I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A tough guy whose physique matters most to him.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hard case' sounds like a tough person; it is a grammatical case notoriously tricky in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is a grammatical case in Latin, and a notoriously hard one for learners.

clue.text: Doctor meant I'm better without a spleen

indicators.note: to doctor letters is to tamper with them and rearrange them
the letter a is left out of the pool before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient tells the doctor they feel better after losing their spleen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spleen' looks like the organ removed, but it means bitter resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen in the old sense of bad temper or resentment is a feeling of bitterness.

clue.text: Brothers' book a reactionary digest

indicators.note: something reactionary goes backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: BROS is the usual abbreviation for brothers

explanation.surface: A siblings' publication is a right-wing digest.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest information is to take it in fully, to absorb it.

clue.text: Count appreciation voiced by America

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so a spelling that sounds the same is used

parts.note: sense is an appreciation or awareness, as in a sense of humour
US is the United States, America

explanation.surface: An aristocratic count expresses gratitude to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman, but it is the noun for a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a population.

clue.text: Site of magnificent mausoleum in simple outline

indicators.note: the city is placed inside the word for simple

parts.note: dim means slow-witted, simple
Agra in India is the site of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A simple sketch of the site of a famous tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simplified drawing showing the outline of something.

clue.text: Creator of Shrek — a massive part in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back, so the run of letters is read backwards
only a part of these words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Looking back, the creator of the film Shrek had a huge role.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker is one who makes or creates something, a creator.

clue.text: Distinguish European news with outside broadcast by the French

parts.note: read as new's, plural of new, giving N twice
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A European news story with a location broadcast is made distinguished by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility, or more generally to distinguish or dignify them.

clue.text: Working both sides of one small stock type of paper

indicators.note: the word for working is placed on either side of the single letter

parts.note: on means working, functioning; it appears twice, one on each side
I is the Roman numeral for one
kin is family, stock or lineage

explanation.surface: A stockbroker works both sides of a small share deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Onionskin is a thin, translucent, lightweight type of paper.

clue.text: Press with spades and clubs

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card game where one presses on holding spades and clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spades and clubs' looks like a pair of card suits, but clubs is the definition: golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are golf clubs with metal heads.

clue.text: Dismiss the odds of green weed capsizing vessel

indicators.note: a capsized vessel is upside down, so the letters are turned backwards
the odd-placed letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Clear away the green weed before the boat capsizes.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'green weed' are REWE, which turned round gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a vessel for water.

clue.text: You may be moved by this role subtly cast

definitions.text: You may be moved by this

indicators.note: letters that are cast are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor is moved by a subtly cast role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' reads as being touched by a performance, but means being carried along.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolleybus is an electric bus powered from overhead wires, which carries passengers.
